name: Adventure Interface Shell
description: A responsive game-interface composition: a router owns screen navigation, style presets provide the visual language, safe-area layout supplies bounded regions, and dedicated sections present title, pause, settings, HUD, objectives, interaction prompts, tooltips, and quick selection. Gameplay systems retain authority for saves, quests, interactions, items, and abilities.

components.role: named visual theme and interface chrome
new game, continue, settings, and quit presentation
modal pause actions and destructive-action confirmation
draft audio, display, control, and accessibility preferences
health, currency, and world-space status projection
world interaction focus and accepted verbs
contextual verb, input glyph, and hold-progress presentation
radial slot focus and selection requests

connections.note: Palette changes resolve through the active named style.
Loaded views receive the router's theme lifecycle.
Navigation closes the wheel without confirming a selection.
Only explicitly applied settings request persistence; draft slider movement does not autosave.

acceptanceCriteria: Route changes produce mutually consistent full-screen sections; title and pause actions remain requests to the session or router API rather than directly mutating gameplay.
Every interactive region remains inside device safe-area insets, compact layouts preserve reachable actions, and touch targets do not fall below the configured minimum.
Theme changes reach every added shell section without any section owning a second palette or interface-style authority; the existing HUD can consume the resolved style through its host API.
Settings edit a draft, emit normalized changes, and request persistence only when explicitly applied; subsystem owners remain responsible for applying values.
Quest tracking is a read-only projection of progression.quest_log and cannot accept, advance, complete, or reward a quest.
Interaction prompts communicate target, verb, availability, input glyph, and hold progress but never execute the interaction.
Tooltips remain within the viewport, quick selection emits at most one selection request per confirmation, and route changes dismiss both without gameplay side effects.
Keyboard, gamepad, pointer, and touch presentations expose equivalent actions; disabled and selected states are not communicated by color alone.
